findings.failure_path: The old workflow required walking the Stage-Entry State Checklist at every stage boundary, and the disposition ledger explicitly retains that trigger. No equivalent survives. Assessment-to-design transitions can therefore proceed without enumerating their prerequisites; first-edit and completion checks do not cover that transition.
findings.smallest_fix: Restore the one-line requirement to load and walk the Stage-Entry State Checklist before every stage transition.

findings.failure_path: The trigger now covers only behavior-changing delivery and requires loading the reference before mapping, rather than before implementation. A claimed mechanical/refactor exemption can avoid the reference entirely, bypassing the exemption classification that the removed Reference Loading rule explicitly required.
findings.smallest_fix: Restore loading before implementation and completion for behavior changes and any implementation claiming a refactor/mechanical exemption.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the ledger requires a new destination section for user-visible notices, but the landing candidate changes only this entrypoint. The deleted text required privacy review of context-derived eligibility, limits on interruption, and protection against stale data implying freshness. Neither that destination nor the other claimed move destinations is supplied, so preservation cannot be established.
findings.smallest_fix: Include the required destination additions in the candidate and supply destination and owner text for checking every move/owner ledger row.

findings.failure_path: A directory-local contract or ADR edit that touches no upstream value set no longer explicitly triggers loading the sync reference. The old rule required that load whenever the owning spec/ADR or nearest contract was updated, and required naming active contract layers before implementation. Both entry obligations are lost.
findings.smallest_fix: Restore contract-layer identification and the reference-load trigger for spec, ADR and repo-contract updates, including directory-local rule changes.

findings.failure_path: Combining the triggers makes every shared-verifier change require a review-altitude technical design before task breakdown. Previously, shared-gate classification and review applied separately; the technical-design artifact required cross-repository, multi-client, external-consumer or high-risk conditions. A narrow verifier repair now gains an additional blocking artifact beyond the conservative redesign.
findings.smallest_fix: Separate shared-gate classification/review from the original conditions that require a technical-design artifact.

findings.failure_path: The unconditional 'results return here' removes the explicit exception allowing standalone non-PRD requirement artifacts to return directly to the user. A standalone current-state inventory or scope artifact now acquires a lifecycle handoff that the previous routing deliberately exempted.
findings.smallest_fix: Limit the return requirement to active deliveries and retain the standalone non-PRD exception.

findings.failure_path: The measured-onboarding trigger now covers developer-facing surfaces without qualification. An existing internal library change that does not affect onboarding, setup, defaults, errors or migration can acquire this gate. The removed rule limited journey proof to new/public surfaces or the listed changes.
findings.smallest_fix: Retain the original triggering conditions in the entrypoint instead of applying journey proof to every developer-facing surface.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: routing rules and pinned text change, but the packet contains no test migrations or current-candidate results. The repository contract requires routing validation and full lanes, while the design also requires phrase-pointer and behavioral checks. Their effectiveness and results cannot be verified from the supplied candidate.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply candidate-bound required validation results, baseline-failure dispositions, and affected test migrations or evidence that no migration is needed.
